title: DDR4 PHY Receiver Front-End
short: A 1.6 Gbps receiver front-end in TSMC 65 nm CMOS with a source-degenerated CTLE.
where: Department of Electrical Engineering, IIT Bombay
summary: At memory and SerDes data rates the channel does a lot of damage before the receiver sees a single bit. This project builds the receiver front-end for a 1.6 Gbps DDR4 PHY in TSMC 65 nm CMOS, starting from a physically realistic model of the FR4 channel and working towards equalization that the channel actually calls for.

I first characterised how FR4 loss changes with trace length, which shows when a receiver can do without equalization and when it cannot. At 1.6 Gbps the loss over 2.5 cm is below 0.02 dB, so short traces need little help. Beyond that regime the CTLE does the work: I designed a source-degenerated CTLE with deliberate pole-zero placement and 8.87 dB of peaking.
resultsNote: Before and after the CTLE, on an 8 m channel.
points: FR4 channel loss measured across trace lengths, giving the length–data-rate regime in which receiver equalization becomes necessary.
Source-degenerated CTLE with pole-zero placement, 8.87 dB peaking.
Next: CTLE–DFE–CDR integration, full-rate transient and BER validation, then layout-parasitic and PVT-corner analysis.

title: First-Principles Study of Monolayer 2H-MoS₂
short: DFT-PBE characterisation of monolayer MoS₂: structure, elasticity, bands, phonons and spin–orbit coupling.
where: Laboratoire des Solides Irradiés (LSI), École Polytechnique, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
summary: A systematic first-principles characterisation of monolayer 2H-MoS₂ using density-functional theory (PBE) in Quantum ESPRESSO. The work covers the structural, elastic, electronic, vibrational and spin–orbit properties of the material, so that each computed quantity can be checked against the others and against the literature.

The elastic constants give a layer incompressibility modulus of about 84 N/m, within roughly 1% of published values, which is the check I used to trust the setup before moving on. The electronic structure shows a direct gap of about 1.68 eV at K, and the phonon dispersion has real frequencies throughout the Brillouin zone, so the structure is dynamically stable at equilibrium. Spin–orbit coupling splits the K-valley valence band by 148 meV, and a maximally-localised Wannier function model reproduces the bands with a few meV of RMS interpolation error.
points: 2D elastic constants and the mechanical properties derived from them.
Band structure and phonon dispersion; no imaginary frequencies, so the structure is dynamically stable.
Spin–orbit coupling and maximally-localised Wannier functions, with few-meV RMS band interpolation error.

title: NUS Young Fellowship Programme
short: Selected for the 2025 programme at the National University of Singapore.
where: NUS Graduate School and SCALE, National University of Singapore
summary: Selected for the 2025 NUS Young Fellowship Programme. The programme combined mentored research tutorials, conversations with faculty and visits to labs across Singapore. I presented a research poster and an oral talk, took part in the 3-Minute Thesis (3MT) challenge, and spent the programme with a cohort from many disciplines who were all weighing research and doctoral paths.
